candidates.source_body_excerpt: A man in his 60s is said to have been hurt following a flat fire in Middleton today. The emergency services were called to the flat on Baguley Crescent shortly after 2.30pm. Three fire engines were scrambled to the scene, and firefighters wearing breathing apparatus tackled a fire in a first-floor flat. It is understood one man, thought to be in his 60s, was hurt. Pictures from the scene showed fire engines and paramedics. An air ambulance also landed nearby. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter A spokesperson for Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service (GMFRS) said: “Just after 2.30pm on Saturday 7 November, fire crews were called to reports of a fire at a residential building on Baguley Crescent, Prestwich . “Three fire engines from Blackley , Whitefield and Broughton stations attended the incident, which involved a first floor flat. "Firefighters wearing breathing apparatus used two hose reels to extinguish the fire. Fire crews remain in attendance alongside other emergency services.” Greater Manchester Police has been approached for comment.

candidates.source_summary: Ian Watson praises Rochdale ‘bravery’ after beating Fleetwood in FA Cup The Northern Echo
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale boss Ian Watson was pleased with his team’s “grit and determination” as they saw off Fleetwood at Highbury for the second time this season to progress into the next round of the FA Cup with a 2-1 win. After Ronan Coughlan’s penalty cancelled out Luke Hannant’s opener for Dale, Baba Adeeko’s strike in the second period of extra time sealed the win which Watson feels will do his side the world of good. He said: “I thought we started the game really well. We’ve been really keen to start to games better. “In recent weeks we’ve started far too slow and it has meant that games have started to get away from us but today we followed our game plan and played with real purpose. “You can tell at the moment we are playing with fear and I really do feel for the lads as that is down to them just wanting to impress so much. So for us to show real grit and determination and some real bravery is really pleasing. “Even into extra time when the lads started to tire, the effort and application was there which was great to see. I really hope we can take some confidence from this win into the next few games.” Fleetwood manager Matt Lawlor was left frustrated after they bowed out of the FA Cup in the first round. He said: “Massively frustrating afternoon. I felt in the first half there was nothing and we let in a poor goal.

candidates.source_title: Lest We Forget: Rochdale battalion's valiant sacrifices during the First World War
candidates.source_summary: From casualties and loss against the Ottomans, to success against the Germans on the Western Front, the Rochdale-based 6th Battalion, Lancashire Fusiliers bravely fought through the First World War, contributing directly to the victory of Britain and the Allies.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: From casualties and loss against the Ottomans, to success against the Germans on the Western Front, the Rochdale-based 6th Battalion, Lancashire Fusiliers bravely fought through the First World War, contributing directly to the victory of Britain and the Allies. Britain declared war on Germany on 4th August 1914, after Germany breached the 1839 Treaty of London by invading Belgium, violating the neutrality of Belgium sworn by the 75 year old multilateral treaty signed by many nations, including the United Kingdom. Later this day, an order was sent to gather men to fight for the posterity of the nation, this was received in Rochdale in the afternoon of that same day that Belgium was invaded. The Rochdale Observer reported that 'a force of 900 men' answered the call to arms, and made way to the Baron Street drill hall. This was a grand shock, with huge crowds gathering, causing a crush that eventuated in the involvement of the police to hold back the crowd. The battalion stayed here until 20th August, when they left early in the morning for a training camp in Turton. The battalion was a unit of the Territorial Force, and was one of the first territorials to be taken overseas, setting sail for Egypt from Southampton on September 25th. They underwent training in Egypt, and joined with other battalions to become the 125th (Lancashire Fusiliers) Brigade in May 1915, before landing at Cape Helles in Gallipoli. The Gallipoli campaign is, unfortunately, remembered as being a failure, resulting in massive casualties and little gains. The 125th Brigade went into action firstly in the loss to the Ottomans at the Second Battle of Krithia, a three day battle that resulted in around a third of the 25,000 Allied soldiers that fought becoming casualties. They then fought at the Third Battle of Krithia and the Battle of Krithia Vineyard, both losses to the Ottomans, where casualties amongst three divisions at the latter battle, including that of the 125th Brigade, where the 6th Battalion, Lancashire Fusiliers were fighting, were 3,469. By August, around two thirds of the Rochdale 6th Battalion, Lancashire Fusiliers had been lost through battle casualties, injuries, sickness, etc. Despite the failure of the Gallipoli campaign, the evacuation is remembered more fondly as an incredibly successful operation, and the remaining members of the 6th Battalion, Lancashire Fusiliers were withdrawn successfully. The 6th Battalion, Lancashire Fusiliers were then transferred to the Western Front, where they saw action at the Third Battle of Ypres, also known as the Battle of Passchendaele, and, in 1918, on the front lines in The Somme, the Battles of Hindenburg Line, and the Final Advance in Picardy, the last campaign being that which forced the surrender of Germany, ending World War 1. Despite the battalion, and the brigade and division it was a part of, receiving immense loss and facing head-to-head with some of the worst battles for the Allies, the Rochdale-based battalion still came out of the war, thought numbers fewer, and were at the front lines during the Final Advance where the Germans eventually surrendered to the Allied forces.

candidates.source_title: Baba Adeeko nets extra-time winner as Rochdale overcome Fleetwood in FA Cup - Fakenham & Wells Times
candidates.source_summary: Baba Adeeko nets extra-time winner as Rochdale overcome Fleetwood in FA Cup Fakenham & Wells Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Substitute Baba Adeeko netted an extra-time winner as Rochdale progressed into the second round of the FA Cup by beating Fleetwood 2-1. Adeeko’s excellent first-time finish six minutes into the second period sent the vocal travelling support into ecstasy and sealed a second win at Highbury this campaign for Dale, following their success in the league back in late September. The hosts created the first clear opening of the game when striker Ronan Coughlan found space in the box but could only blaze a shot harmlessly over Sam Waller’s goal. Rochdale then took the lead after 23 minutes. Some slick one-touch football saw captain Harvey Gilmour combine with Charlie Tasker to set up Luke Hannant, who tapped in a neat first-time finish at the far post past Jay Lynch. Fleetwood pressed for an equaliser in the second half and went close when Harrison Neal’s effort from outside the box had to be gathered at the second attempt by Waller. The Cod Army levelled things up going into the last quarter of normal time thanks to a Coughlan penalty after Aaron Loupalo-Bi was hauled to the ground by Kaiden Wilson. Both teams went close in extra time before Adeeko’s winner, with Dale sub Bryant Bilongo failing to convert Tasker’s cross before Danny Andrew stung the palms of Waller with a well-struck free-kick.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Substitute Baba Adeeko netted an extra-time winner as Rochdale progressed into the second round of the FA Cup by beating Fleetwood 2-1. Adeeko’s excellent first-time finish six minutes into the second period sent the vocal travelling support into ecstasy and sealed a second win at Highbury this campaign for Dale, following their success in the league back in late September. The hosts created the first clear opening of the game when striker Ronan Coughlan found space in the box but could only blaze a shot harmlessly over Sam Waller’s goal. Rochdale then took the lead after 23 minutes. Some slick one-touch football saw captain Harvey Gilmour combine with Charlie Tasker to set up Luke Hannant, who tapped in a neat first-time finish at the far post past Jay Lynch. Fleetwood pressed for an equaliser in the second half and went close when Harrison Neal’s effort from outside the box had to be gathered at the second attempt by Waller. The Cod Army levelled things up going into the last quarter of normal time thanks to a Coughlan penalty after Aaron Loupalo-Bi was hauled to the ground by Kaiden Wilson. Both teams went close in extra time before Adeeko’s winner, with Dale sub Bryant Bilongo failing to convert Tasker’s cross before Danny Andrew stung the palms of Waller with a well-struck free-kick.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A school has changed its name to better reflect the community it serves. Children at the Middleton primary school formed a giant star in their playground as they celebrated their school’s new name with a special visit from the Bishop of Middleton. Rhodes Green Church of England Primary School — previously known as Little Heaton CE Primary School — welcomed the Rt Revd Mark Davies on Thursday for a day of celebrations attended by pupils, staff, parents and members of the local community. The school, in Boardman Lane in Rhodes, officially changed its name in September as part of a fresh chapter under headteacher Chloe Noon. The new name reflects the school’s connection to the Rhodes community, where many of its children live and grow up, while its renewed identity is built around the Christian vision Shine as stars in the world. To mark the occasion, children gathered in the playground to form a giant star, captured in a photograph taken from above. Bishop Mark was also given a tour by the school’s head boy and head girl, visiting classrooms and meeting children from every year group before joining families for a special assembly. He has also been disqualified from diving for six years and two months. CCTV footage showed Grainger consuming several alcoholic drinks before returning to his car at 3.25am. Concerned by his behaviour as he approached the car, CCTV operators alerted police that a man who appeared intoxicated was preparing to get behind the wheel and drive away. Officers were provided with a description of the vehicle, its registration number and the location it was leaving from. When officers attempted to stop the Seat Leon as it left the town centre, Grainger failed to stop and a short pursuit commenced.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A man has been jailed after leading police on a high-speed chase through Rochdale after an evening of drinking before crashing into a pedestrian. Cameron Grainger was sentenced at Manchester Crown Court on Friday (November 6) after being found guilty of causing serious injury by dangerous driving. The court heard that on November 19, 2023, Grainger parked his Seat Leon in Upper Broadfield Car Park in Rochdale town centre before spending nearly three hours drinking in nearby bars with friends. CCTV footage showed him consuming several alcoholic drinks before returning to his car around 3.25am. Concerned by his behaviour, CCTV operatores alerted police that an apparently intoxicated man was about to drive away. When police attempted to stop Grainger, from Rochdale, as he left the town centre, he continued driving and a pursuit began. The 25-year-old drove at speed along Rochdale Road, repeatedly crossing onto the wrong side of the road. The chase ended when Grainger struck a now 41-year-old pedestrian, with police stopping to provide first aid to the man who had suffered serious injuries.

candidates.source_summary: Middleton’s regeneration has taken another major step forward with the council formally completing the purchase of Warwick Mill from developer Kam Lei Fong.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Middleton’s regeneration has taken another major step forward with the council formally completing the purchase of Warwick Mill from developer Kam Lei Fong. Once a thriving cotton mill, the imposing structure, which was built in 1907, has been vacant for at least a decade and has since become an eyesore, regularly attracting vandalism and urban explorers. The council sees redevelopment of Warwick Mill, which is Grade II listed, as a major opportunity to bring an important historic building back into use as new homes for the benefit of the Middleton community. The neighbouring 1960s office block, London House, has also been purchased as part of the £3.3 million deal, with plans to demolish the building. Work to transform the building will get under way quickly. Rochdale firm Winterburns is set to take over security immediately, with a beefed up, 24-hour presence on site. The firm will also start clearing the mountain of debris which has built up over years of neglect, including 1,000 tyres and overgrown plants and trees. Teams will soon start the delicate internal strip out of Warwick Mill and London House. The demolition of London House, a brutalist structure with little architectural merit, is set to get under way early in the New Year. The council will then kick start the process of tendering a developer partner to undertake the longer-term work of bringing Warwick Mill back into use.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Doncaster Rovers has backed defender Sean Grehan to grow into a ‘top-class’ footballer and has given the youngster plenty of words of encouragement. Grehan has established himself as a regular starter this season after being a slightly more peripheral figure at times last term. However, the Republic of Ireland Under-21 captain, who played the full 90 minutes of Rovers’ 6-1 loss to MK Dons, was substituted at half-time during the 4-1 win over Rochdale after a clumsy error which allowed veteran Ian Henderson to open the scoring after 15 minutes. “Sean's top. He's going to be top-class,” McCann told the Free Press. “He's 21 years of age.I said to him after the game, ‘I don't ever want you to stop making those types of passes. I want you to keep that sort of bravery about you.’ “He's made a mistake because he tried to break a line with a pass.I'm OK with that. I'm fine. We're all human at the end of the day.We make mistakes.” “If I said that to my centre-halves, we wouldn't have seen the pass from Jay McGrath for the second goal or the unbelievable split in the lines with passes. I want my centre-backs to be brave. “So, he'll probably do it again. Hopefully it doesn't lead to a goal against us. And Jay will do it and Byrne will do it and Matty will do it. But I want them to be brave. And that's the most important thing.” McCann also explained that the decision to take off Grehan at half-time had always been in his mind heading into the Rochdale match due to the amount of minutes that the defender has played recently. He said: “With Sean, I just said, ‘look, don't be down because of that. Do it again. Make sure you're better with your execution the next time.’ “We're always going to make substitutions at half-time. Sean was always in the head, particularly after playing the whole game on a Saturday. So, it was more of a rotational game, really, the Rochdale game.”

Our pathology teams process more than 10 million samples and perform over 35 million tests every year, supporting patients across Greater Manchester and beyond. While patients may never meet the professionals working in pathology laboratories, their role is critical. In fact, around 95% of clinical pathways rely on pathology services, providing the diagnostic information clinicians need to diagnose illness, guide treatment and monitor ongoing care. At the heart of this work colleagues are combining scientific expertise with the latest technology to deliver faster, more efficient testing for patients. Earlier this year, the Oldham laboratory introduced new automated biopsy processing technology designed to support specimen preparation around the clock. The system can operate 24 hours a day, seven days a week, helping improve workflow, create additional capacity and enable biomedical scientists to spend more time on highly specialised diagnostic work. The introduction of the technology builds on a wider programme of innovation within the laboratory, which has also led the way in adopting digital pathology, allowing specialists to review biopsy samples digitally and collaborate more easily across healthcare organisations. The past year has also seen colleagues successfully implement a new Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) across pathology services. The major programme has transformed how laboratories manage samples and results, with teams across all sites working together to ensure services for patients continued uninterrupted throughout the transition. The NCA's pathology workforce includes almost 700 colleagues working across Oldham, Salford, Rochdale, Bury, Wigan, Wrightington and Leigh. Together they represent a diverse range of professions including biomedical scientists, pathologists, clinical scientists, mortuary practitioners, biomedical support workers, transfusion practitioners, microbiologists, virologists, biochemists, point of care testing teams, administrators, porters and messengers.

Lewis Mahoney applied to Rochdale Council for retrospective planning permission to remove the original boundary wall and raised beds to create a new garden wall and 1.8m high timber fencing at 1 Bates Close, Rochdale. But the changes to the corner plot have drawn criticism from the council’s planning department. A planning officer’s report said: “The application proposes the retention of a 1.8m high close-boarded fence which has been constructed adjacent to the public footpath at the boundary of the site without the benefit of planning permission. The original boundary wall at 1 Bates Close. Image: Google “The surrounding street scene is characterised by an absence of hard boundary treatment; most dwellings open directly to the public footpath, and in cases where there is boundary treatment, this is characterised by low-rise timber fencing or similar. “The proposed 1.8m high boundary fencing would therefore be at odds with this established character and would appear as an incongruous, out-of-character addition to the street scene which would be detrimental to the established character of the street scene. “The site location on the junction of Bates Close and hard against the public footpath would mean that the development would be readily visible from the public realm and surrounding dwellings and would read as an oppressive and intrusive form of development.

This free-to-attend night-time event will run for three evenings, Friday, November 20 to Sunday, November 22, 2026, and be open from 5pm to 8pm. Organiser Rochdale Development Agency is promising new dazzling trails and attractions to make it the best yet. Taking centre stage is the Body, which takes visitors on a journey through six zones of the human body using fire, light, sound and special effects. The multi-sensory experience is Walk the Plank's most ambitious fire-and-light installation, from multi-award-winning outdoor arts specialists. Having previously travelled across the globe, from Ireland to Canada Ignite Fire Festival will see its north-west premiere. Audiences can expect to be mesmerised on this dramatic, spellbinding journey as they walk through the glowing embers of human metabolism - the silent furnace that keeps us alive, continuously generating heat to power all the body's functions. Using cutting-edge technology, the experience will entertain and educate, providing a deeper understanding of what lies beneath. Bev Ayre, senior producer at Walk the Plank, said: "The countdown is on until we bring Body to Ignite and we can't wait. We hope our dynamic fire and light installation will not only entertain audiences but also inspire everyone to learn more about what makes us all human. We’re also excited to illuminate the slopes and gardens with fire and special effects, framing the beautiful town hall."

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A homeowner faces having to tear down a garden fence because of the impact it has on the neighbouring area. Rochdale Council refused Caterina Buonocore’s application for retrospective planning permission for the 1.55m high boundary fence — about twice the height of the original — around 19 Town House Road, Littleborough. She appealed that decision. But yesterday, a Planning Inspector rejected the appeal, stating: “The main issue is the effect of the appeal development on the character and appearance of the area. “Boundary treatments in the area are typically low-level and visually permeable, contributing to a sense of openness and allowing the soft landscaping within front gardens to remain appreciable. The existing greenery helps to soften the street scene and makes a positive contribution to the character and appearance of the area. “The appeal development introduces a close-boarded timber fence. The height, materials and extensive continuous form of enclosure contrasts with the more open and traditional forms of boundary treatment typically found in the locality. “On site, I observed that due to the prominent corner location, when seen from Park View against the back drop of traditional stone terraces with low-key forms of boundary treatment, the appeal development appears particularly stark and incongruous within the street scene. candidates.source_summary: 'Terrific at times' - Cliff Byrne's assessment of Doncaster Rovers' performance against Rochdale Doncaster Free Press
candidates.source_body_excerpt: It was Jersey Mike’s delight for Doncaster Rovers, who came back from behind to secure a thumping 4-1 victory away at Rochdale. There was nine changes made from the team that were hammered by MK Dons on Saturday, with Brandon Hanlan marking his return to the starting lineup with his first goal this season, in an evening which also saw Alfie May, Owen Bailey and Isaac Hutchinson all add to their tallies for the season. Cliff Byrne said: “At the start, we wanted to secure our place in the next round. I think the level of the performance tonight was terrific at times. It was exhilarating. I know we didn’t have many fans in the stadium tonight but the ones that were here I think will appreciate that.” Rovers came from behind to secure the victory, marking the first time the team has managed that across all competitions since beating Rotherham United on derby day back in February. Sean Grehan was at fault for Rochdale’s opener in a challenging evening for the young defender, who was replaced by Owen Bailey at half-time. He added: “We did conceded from an error and our behalf and we got punished for it. I think over the course of the game we had a lot of control and we showed in particular during the second-half a lot of calmness in the top end of the pitch, which resulted in the four goals.” Reflecting on his team’s spirit along with the first-half error, Byrne added: “We ask the players to play a particular way and we give them autonomy within that to be flexible within the guidelines of how we like to play. Sometimes mistakes can happen and it’s important that we don’t be overly critical because we want players to take opportunites and we want them to be risk takers as well. “It’s important that the whole group contribute and I think we’ve seen that tonight.”

candidates.source_summary: 'Played with intent', 'A true captain's performance': Doncaster Rovers player ratings from EFL Trophy win at Rochdale Doncaster Free Press
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Doncaster Rovers came from behind to secure a well-deserved 4-1 victory away at Rochdale, securing their place in the knockout stages of the EFL Trophy in the process. Grant McCann made nine changes from the team that was thrashed away at MK Dons on Saturday. Josh Clarke was selected in goal, Jay McGrath and Tom Nixon returned to the defence while there was also opportunities for the likes of Harry Clifton, Darren Robinson, Bayley McCann and Brandon Hanlan among others. Jack Senior and Sean Grehan were the only players to keep their place in the starting lineup. Doncaster Rovers got off to a challenging start and were forced into an early change after just three minutes when new arrival Will Keane was forced off with an injury. Hanlan could and probably should have put Rovers in the driving seat moments later, but was denied by a strong save by Sam Waller. Matters got worse after 15 minutes when the hosts took an early lead, latching on to a mistake from Sean Grehan, which allowed Ian Henderson to easily tap home from close-range on his record-breaking 532nd appearance for the Dale. McCann’s men made more changes at the break, introducing both Owen Bailey and Jordan Thomas in an effort to rejuvenate their hopes of progressing to the next stage of the competition and it very much worked the trick. Rovers levelled proceedings in the 54th minute through Alfie May’s close distance strike after great work from Clifton in the build-up. The Vikings then the took the lead nine minutes later when Hanlan netted his first of the season from close range after some brilliant work by both McGrath and Thomas. Bailey, who was brought on to play centre-back in the second half, put the game to bed with a close-range finish in the 88th minute, capping off a true captain’s performance from the 27-year-old. Subsitute Isaac Hutchinson then topped off a great day for the visitors with a goal from close distance. Here are our player ratings from Doncaster Rovers’ final EFL Trophy group stage game.
